en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Seventh Chapter
Discussion on Mental Factors:
Is there no mental state (dhamma) that is mental?
Yes, [there is].

Is it not the case that there are certain phenomena which are co-existent with consciousness, conascent, conjoined, associated, arising together, ceasing together, having the same basis, and having the same object?
Yes, they exist.

If indeed there are certain phenomena which are co-existent with consciousness, conascent, conjoined, associated, arising together, ceasing together, having the same basis, and having the same object, then surely, alas, you should not say [that consciousness is dissociated from them].
“There is no mental state.
Is contact co-nascent with consciousness? Yes.
If contact is co-nascent with consciousness, then indeed, O sir, it must be said:
"Contact is mental. Feeling... [and so on].
perception … volition … faith …
Energy … mindfulness … concentration …
Wisdom … lust … hatred …
Is delusion … pe … lack of moral dread conascent with the mind? Yes.
If non-shame is co-nascent with consciousness, then indeed, O friend, you must say:
"Non-shame is a mental factor.
Is it because it is co-nascent with consciousness that it is called a mental factor?
“Yes.
“Since they are co-nascent with contact, are they ‘contact-born’?
“Yes.”
Is it because they are co-nascent with the mind that they are called mental factors?
Yes. [The same applies to] feeling...
of perception … of volition … of faith …
By means of energy … by means of mindfulness … by means of concentration …
... by means of wisdom ...
by means of lust ...
by means of hatred ...
Is it because it is co-nascent with delusion … pe … and with lack of moral dread that it is called "accompanied by lack of moral dread"?
Yes, it is.
"There is no mental state"?
Yes, [you say].
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Indeed, this mind and mental phenomena are experienced as non-self;
having understood both the inferior and the sublime within these two, [one should train].”
“The one with right vision knows that things are subject to disintegration.
Is this indeed a sutta? Yes.
"In that case, there is a mental state (cetasika-dhamma).
"Is it not the case that there is no mental state?
"Yes."
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Here, Kevaṭṭa, a bhikkhu declares the mind of other beings, of other persons; he declares their mental factors; he declares their thoughts;
he declares their reflections: ‘Such is your mind, such is your mind, such is your consciousness.’”
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, there exists a mental state (cetasika-dhamma).
The Discussion of Mental Factors is finished.
